claim: A page-level embedding field exists that stores a vector capturing the page's content.
reason: Field existence only; module placement is as quoted by the author, verify in hexdocs. How or whether it is used is not in the docs.

claim: Site-level embedding fields (site2vec, plus an encoded/compressed form) exist in the NSR data module.
reason: Names corroborated independently by mojodojo (site2vecEmbeddingEncoded).

claim: siteScore provides an aggregated site-level quality score.
reason: Wording 'aggregated' is the author's; check the attribute's own description. Existence is not proof of ranking use.

claim: siteFocusScore quantifies how focused a site is on a particular topic.
reason: Author places it in QualityAuthorityTopicEmbeddingsVersionedItem; mojodojo places it under nsrDataProto/QualityNSR. Resolve the module in hexdocs before citing a path. Definition itself is corroborated by mojodojo.

claim: siteRadius measures how far individual pages deviate from the site's central theme.
reason: Same module-placement discrepancy as siteFocusScore; definition corroborated by mojodojo.

claim: Site vectors seem to be only 64 dimensions (quoted from Mike King: 'kinda shocked me considering so many of the other embeddings models are much higher dimensionality').
reason: Recycled from Mike King, not original. Checkable against the attribute description; do not cite beyond 'reported by King'.

claim: Embeddings are versioned via versionId.
reason: Trivial structural fact, low value.

claim: Frame-level image embeddings exist in the docs.
reason: Existence only; irrelevant to local-SEO work.

modules: NlpSaftEntity (entityType, entityTypeProbability, gender, name); NlpSemanticParsingSaftMentionAnnotation; NlpSaftAnnotatedPhrase; NlpSaftLabeledSpan
claim: SAFT identifies named entities (PER, ORG, LOC) and annotates arbitrary spans in a document.
reason: Restates module descriptions; shows an entity-typing NLP stack exists. Says nothing about ranking.

claim: SAFT resolves pronouns and nominal mentions to their entities.
reason: Doc-description restatement.

claim: SAFT defines relations between entities in a document.
reason: Doc-description restatement.

claim: SAFT represents semantic constructions as a directed acyclic graph.
reason: Doc-description restatement.

modules: NlpSaftEntityProfile; NlpSaftToken (tag, lemma); NlpSaftMorphology; NlpSemanticParsingSaftMeasure; NlpSaftDocument; VideoContentSearchSaftEntityInfo
claim: An entity profile holds canonical names, attributes and embeddings for one entity, and SAFT integrates with Google's Knowledge Vault for entity fusion/linkage.
reason: Knowledge Vault linkage is the author's reading of module text; verify the specific attribute before repeating it.

claim: Embeddings could be used for finding similar content, evaluating quality, detecting spam, and tracking site change over time.
reason: Author labels it 'totally speculative' ('I'm not saying this is how it's used'). No basis in the docs.

claim: Detailed 'inferred architecture', component interactions and data-flow diagram of how SAFT feeds Google Search.
reason: Author states it is a constructed 'theoretical product' and 'a long shot'. Discard as fact.

claim: No SEO recommendations; the value of the leak is a shared vocabulary rather than confirmed ranking factors.
reason: Honest framing, useful as a calibration of how to treat the docs. Author is the most careful of the six; mostly original structured walk-through, with King as the only recycled element (also names Fishkin, Goodwin).

claim: NavBoost has collected and analysed clickstream data since the mid-2000s; long clicks vs short clicks are 'pivotal' to relevance and ranking.
reason: Recycled from Fishkin/King. Keep: NavBoost exists and is click-derived. Discard: 'pivotal' (a weight claim the docs cannot support).

claim: Google uses Chrome user data to assess page popularity/relevance and high Chrome engagement 'can significantly boost' rankings.
reason: 'Significantly boost' is an asserted ranking weight. Recycled from King; docs only show Chrome-derived fields.

claim: topUrl uses Chrome click data to identify a site's most important pages for sitelinks.
reason: Recycled from King. Plausible doc-text restatement; verify attribute description.

claim: EWOK lets human quality raters give feedback that is 'directly integrated' into search algorithms.
reason: Keep: EWOK/rater platform referenced in docs (King). Discard 'directly integrated': not shown.

claim: Google keeps whitelists for sectors such as travel, COVID-19 and elections.
reason: Recycled from King (no attribute names given here). Presence of sector flags is doc-based; 'ensures credible sources' is speculation. Not relevant to local service SEO.

claim: Click data is segmented by geography and device type.
reason: Attribute names are not corroborated by the other five sources; verify in hexdocs before use.

claim: Established brands receive preferential treatment in rankings; domain- and query-level interaction boosts sites that satisfy intent.
reason: Asserts a ranking effect with no attribute and no docs basis.

claim: These click attributes exist and capture user engagement with results.
reason: Names recycled from King's post. Keep existence only; 'influencing ranking decisions' is not shown.

claim: Quality scores are derived from engagement metrics and human rater feedback.
reason: Attribute names not corroborated; the derivation is invented. Probable AI-assisted embellishment (site advertises a Leak Help GPT).

claim: Measures how well a result satisfies intent, driven by clicks, engagement and feedback.
reason: Name uncorroborated; mechanism not documented.

claim: These track navigation through results and inform ranking adjustments.
reason: Names uncorroborated by other sources; 'informs ranking' is an assertion. Verify before reuse.

claim: Attributes indicate how Google mitigates spam, penalising high-score sites.
reason: Generic names uncorroborated; penalty claim not shown. mojodojo's uacSpamScore is the verifiable spam attribute.

claim: Docs were accidentally exposed on GitHub between March and May 2024, distributed via Hexdocs.
reason: Corroborated by Okoone; consistent with the package being hosted on hexdocs.

claim: Former Google employees reviewed the docs and found them authentic (anonymous, initial review).
reason: Author hedges ('reports suggest'); hearsay but widely repeated.

claim: Anonymous source identified as Erfan Azimi (29 May update).
reason: Public fact, corroborated by Okoone.

claim: Recommendations: speed/mobile, Chrome-insight page optimisation, content audits, GBP and reviews, brand PR, backlink monitoring.
reason: Generic advice dressed as leak implications; adds nothing checkable. Source overall is recycled from iPullRank (cited in references), no original analysis.

claim: Leak spans 2,500+ pages and 14,014 attributes in the 'Content API Warehouse'; docs do not specify attribute weights.
reason: Scale and the no-weights caveat are the most useful lines in the piece and match Fishkin/King.

claim: Docs were accidentally public on GitHub March-May 2024; Fishkin reported it, Azimi was the source.
reason: Provenance, corroborated by Dealers League.

claim: Chrome was built to collect full clickstream data to improve results.
reason: Recycled from King; motive/history, not something the attribute docs state.

claim: NavBoost collects click patterns and trending-search data that Google uses to adjust rankings.
reason: Existence keeps; the 'secret weapon' framing and use in production are not proven by the docs.

claim: 'Leaked documents confirm' click and engagement data are significant ranking factors.
reason: 'Confirm' and 'significant' assert weight and production use; docs prove fields exist only.

claim: A siteAuthority attribute exists.
reason: Field existence is real (reported by King). Google has said it has no 'domain authority'; the docs do not say how the value is used.

claim: A higher siteAuthority 'significantly boosts the rankings' of a site's pages.
reason: Asserted ranking weight with no doc support.

claim: Google uses CTR and user interactions to adjust rankings.
reason: Stated as confirmed; no attribute cited.

claim: New or suspected spammy sites are placed in a sandbox until they build credibility.
reason: No attribute cited. The only sandbox-adjacent attribute is hostAge, and mojodojo reads it as fresh-spam handling, not a new-domain sandbox.

claim: User-generated content quality and engagement metrics feed Google's content-quality evaluation.
reason: No attribute cited.

claim: Personalisation and machine learning continuously refine rankings.
reason: Generic and unrelated to anything specific in the leak.

claim: Dwell time and long clicks are indicators of valuable content that can improve rankings.
reason: No attribute named (lastLongestClicks exists elsewhere); effect on ranking asserted.

claim: Google gives priority to video content in rankings.
reason: No basis cited; docs show nothing of the sort in this article.

claim: Link juice and PageRank sculpting are no longer in use 'according to the leaked documents'.
reason: No attribute cited and contradicted by mojodojo, who counts four Pagerank fields with comments as recent as late 2022 (a deprecated flag on one does not retire the concept).

claim: Leak contradicts public Google statements, e.g. Gary Illyes saying clicks do not influence rankings.
reason: Reasonable framing: click-derived fields exist (NavBoost family) in tension with public statements. Does not prove production use or weight.

claim: Ten recommendations: authority/backlinks, titles and CTR, patience with new sites, UGC, personalisation, structured data, video with geotags, independent A/B testing.
reason: Generic; several rest on discarded claims. Piece is almost entirely recycled from Fishkin and King with no attribute-level analysis.

claim: CompositeDoc collects all information about a document, comparable to the on-page data for a URL.
reason: Restates the module's purpose.

claim: CompositeDoc 'clearly defines all attributes of On-page SEO and what is and is not important for a URL'.
reason: Overreach: the module lists fields, not importance.

claim: CompressedQualitySignals is a model that feeds into Google systems.
reason: Cited with no detail here; see DL/OK for the click-signal fields reported by King.

claim: Mustang scores, ranks and returns results using input from several models, with an underlying ranking algorithm called AScorer.
reason: System names appear in doc comments (also in King's post); the description of the scoring role is inference from those comments.

claim: TeraGoogle is an indexing system storing the recent processed corpus for retrieval.
reason: System named in doc comments; description is inferred.

claim: Amarna is referenced in SafesearchVideoContentSignals.
reason: Bare reference, low value.

claim: Raffia is probably an indexing system ('some references indicate').
reason: Author hedges; low confidence.

claim: PerDocData is a protocol buffer used for indexing and serving; the author's notes are a 'cursory analysis'.
reason: Structural fact, appropriately labelled cursory.

claim: scienceDoctype classifies science documents: <0 not science, 0 fully visible, >0 limited visibility (number of visible terms).
reason: Doc-comment restatement; not relevant to local SEO.

claim: uacSpamScore is a value 0-127 where above 64 indicates spam.
reason: Presented as comment text; verify the scale and threshold in hexdocs. Existence plus a stated scale, not a demotion rule.

claim: spamtokensContentScore measures user-generated-content spam and is used in SiteBoostTwiddler.
reason: Verify the 'used in' link in the attribute description.

claim: OriginalContentScore runs 0-127 for little-content pages and up to 512 for actual originality score; 'little content' is undefined and may be relative.
reason: Ranges are doc-text as presented; the 'relative' reading is the author's flagged hypothesis. Author correctly notes the definition is missing.

claim: 'Originality may be rewarded and closely related to topical authority.'
reason: No doc basis.

claim: PerDocData stores several freshness signals: freshbox classifier scores, date-component confidence, page-age dates, a deprecated encoded field, and last significant update.
reason: Doc-text restatement of what is stored. Highly relevant to the refresh workflow as proof the fields exist.

claim: 'Content freshness looks like a key factor' and regular updates earn a freshness boost.
reason: Key-factor and boost claims are ranking-weight assertions; many fields prove storage only.

claim: Mobile-specific per-document fields exist: smartphone optimisation, desktop-error/mobile-ok mismatch, flash ratio.
reason: Doc-text as presented; descriptions unverified. isWebErrorMobileContent phrasing carries the author's own question mark.

claim: A boolean flags mobile-interstitial violations and demotes the page when set.
reason: The 'demotes' wording is presented as doc-text; consistent with Google's public interstitial policy. Refresh timing claim ('no way to know if and when this refreshes') is not in the docs.

claim: Four PageRank attributes exist (one deprecated, three undocumented); comments as new as late 2022 mean 'pagerank is well and alive'.
reason: Keep the four-field fact. 'Alive' is inference from comment dates, which show maintenance not use in ranking.

claim: Hacked-site signals exist and are used in query-time joins, which likely demote affected pages.
reason: Fields and join usage are doc-based; the demotion is the author's own 'likely'.

claim: nsrDataProto leads to QualityNSR, a model of stripped-down site-level signals.
reason: Structural fact; corroborated by MarketMuse using the same family (QualityNsrNsrData).

claim: titlematchScore signals how well titles match the user query.
reason: Definition as presented; 'extremely important' is a weight claim and is discarded.

claim: A compressed site embedding exists, likely used for site theme and topical clustering.
reason: Existence corroborated by MarketMuse; use is flagged 'likely'.

claim: Higher siteFocusScore means more topic concentration; siteRadius shows how far a page strays from the site topic.
reason: Definitions corroborated by MarketMuse.

claim: 'Higher concentration leads to higher authority', so prune off-topic content.
reason: Effect on ranking is not shown; the pruning advice is a recommendation the docs do not support.

claim: A numeric small-personal-site promotion score exists, likely promoting small blogs.
reason: Field exists; the 'promotion of small blogs' reading is inference.

claim: hostAge is the earliest firstseen date across pages on a host, used in a twiddler to 'sandbox fresh spam in serving time'.
reason: Doc-text restatement, and the author correctly reads it as spam handling rather than a new-domain sandbox (his own labelled opinion).

claim: If host_age equals domain_age, domain_age is omitted, so changing hosts restarts the clock.
reason: Inference from a comment fragment; treat 'resets on host change' as unproven.

claim: badSslCertificate checks for a bad SSL certificate or a redirect chain and feeds back into CompositeDoc.
reason: Verify the exact description; effect on ranking not stated.

claim: tofu is a site-level quality predictor based on site content.
reason: Description only; the 'keep top-of-funnel users happy' tip is the author's own question mark and is discarded.

claim: impressions likely stores total site impressions and feeds perDocData, 'which indicates that impressions play a role in rankings'.
reason: Ranking-role inference from a field's data flow, which proves existence only.

claim: clutterScore is a site-level delta signal for distracting/annoying resources, with a comment about 'penalizing sites with a large number of distracting/annoying resources'.
reason: Comment text is doc-based; 'explicit penalty' is interpretation, and the author admits the resource definition is missing.

claim: contentEffort is an LLM-based effort estimate for article pages; unclear if it detects LLM text or scores effort.
reason: Doc text with the ambiguity honestly flagged.

claim: rhubarb is a site-URL delta quality score computed in Goldmine via the Rhubarb model; unversionedRhubarb is the URL-level delta.
reason: Doc-text restatement.

modules: CompositeDoc.LocalWWWInfo (address, brickAndMortarStrength, geotopicality, isLargeChain, isLargeLocalwwwinfo, siteSiblings)
claim: The local info model carries address, a float brick-and-mortar strength, geotopicality, chain and large-site booleans and sibling-site count; notes say these are per-document signals independent of a specific address.
reason: Highest-value material for local SEO; doc-text restatement of field types and the independence note.

claim: WrapptorItem keeps the address footprint (address, phone, business name), which essentially 'validates the NAP'.
reason: Fields are doc-based; 'validates NAP' and the NAP advice are inference.

claim: isLargeLocalwwwinfo 'likely provides a boost for larger sites'.
reason: Boost is asserted from a boolean's existence.

claim: Docs hosted on hexdocs.pm as Elixir modules named GoogleApi.ContentWarehouse.V1.Model.*, protobuf-derived; the author says it is an 'ongoing' 'cursory analysis' and that comments run as new as late 2022; no weights, code or thresholds are given, and key terms (little content, distracting resources) are undefined.
reason: Raw page states no version number, module count or namespace tally; those the first fetch summary reported (e.g. version 0.4.0) were not in the page text. Treat structural statistics as absent.

claim: Seirdy's linked post argues the SEO hype around the leak is overblown and that readers should focus on 'agent optimization' over SEO (thread shows only this one-line summary of the post).
reason: The thread is a pointer; the substance is in Seirdy's own article (not fetched, not in the assigned list). Opinion, not a leak claim.

claim: Brad: agent optimisation rather than SEO suits the non-commercial web long term.
reason: Opinion unrelated to leak content.

claim: Colin (Mojeek): the truncation limit the post discusses may apply to embeddings and may not apply, or may differ, for keyword search.
reason: Search-engine-builder inference, explicitly hedged ('perhaps', 'may'). No attribute name given in the thread.

claim: Colin, relaying Marc: Google and Mojeek have always had a maximum page size, which would explain the truncation, though he expects a different limit for embeddings.
reason: The Mojeek fact is first-hand; applying it to Google is inference. Only builder-perspective content on the page. No module counts, namespaces or versions appear anywhere in the thread.

claim: The leak comprises 'some 3000 internal documents'.
reason: Contradicts the 2,500+ pages and 14,014 attributes in Okoone/Fishkin/King; unsourced figure.

claim: The leak is both a technical tool for engineers and a manual for managing content data.
reason: Loose but harmless description of an API-docs package.

modules: none cited (patent 'Framework for evaluating web search scoring functions')
claim: Google runs different ranking systems by sector (travel, commerce) and picks which to show after processing.
reason: Rests on a patent title and SERP observation, not on the leak; patent not verified.

claim: An internal link carries a pagerankWeight of 0.87, so authority transfers through links.
reason: Names are not documented in other sources; the snippet value reads as illustrative. Presents a number as a ranking weight.

claim: Google assigns a relevance_score of 0.76 to a link from a fuzzy anchor-to-page match.
reason: No such module or attribute is corroborated; the numeric score is unverifiable and looks invented.

claim: Module restricts content by user region (example: restricted in FR, allowed in US/CA), proving Google filters by geo rules for UX.
reason: Module name is not corroborated here and it concerns abuse-policy restriction, not local ranking; the local-SEO application is speculation.

claim: Module filters underage users from sensitive content.
reason: Same: unverified here and unrelated to organic ranking.

claim: Poorly structured metadata leads to incomplete indexing and lower visibility; metadata optimisation is crucial for fast indexing.
reason: No attribute named; generic claim.

claim: A built-in NLP algorithm assigns a semantic relevance score from contextual_entities.
reason: Name uncorroborated; contrast with real NlpSaft* modules documented by MarketMuse.

claim: Recommendations: internal links from high-traffic pages, anchors like 'Pest Extermination in Repentigny', multimodal image metadata.
reason: Generic and tied to unverifiable snippets. Promotional client-case framing; not original leak analysis.

claim: Fetch method and fidelity notes.
reason: OK, DL, BC, MD, MJ read via raw fetch tool; MM blocked raw fetch (403) and was read through WebFetch summaries, so MM quotes are summariser-extracted. BC code snippets appear to be images and were not captured as text. The first WebFetch pass for MD and MJ contained facts absent from the raw page (e.g. version 0.4.0, a not-present list); raw text was used instead.

claim: Source quality ranking.
reason: Best to worst: MD (original attribute-level reading, flags its own gaps, but several 'ranking factor' leaps and one 'Pro Tip' per section) > MM (original but self-declared speculation beyond field names) > MJ (a pointer thread, almost no content) > OK and DL (recycled Fishkin/King, assert weights) > BC (unverifiable snippets, likely invented values). None of the six is a primary source; verify every attribute in hexdocs before use.
